articles.title: Tourism Growth in India
articles.snippet: Explore how India is transforming into a global tourism hub through heritage, infrastructure, digital initiatives, sustainable tourism, government schemes,...
articles.fullTextHtml:
03 Aug 2026

Explore how India is transforming into a global tourism hub through heritage, infrastructure, digital initiatives, sustainable tourism, government schemes, and inclusive economic growth.

Syllabus Areas:

GS I - Culture

GS II - Governance

GS III - Economy

India is rapidly emerging as a leading global tourism destination by leveraging its rich cultural heritage, natural diversity, spiritual traditions, wellness ecosystem, and improved tourism infrastructure. The Government is promoting tourism as an engine of economic growth, employment generation, community participation, and sustainable development.

Tourism as a Growth Engine

Tourism has become one of India's fastest-growing economic sectors and contributes significantly to employment, regional development and livelihood generation.

Major Tourism Segments

1. Spiritual and Pilgrimage Tourism

India attracts millions of pilgrims every year through:

  • Char Dham

  • Kashi

  • Ayodhya

  • Tirupati

  • Amritsar

  • Puri

Improved connectivity and visitor facilities have strengthened India's position as a spiritual tourism destination.

2. Buddhist Circuit Tourism

The Buddhist Circuit connects important sites associated with Lord Buddha and attracts pilgrims from across Asia and the world, strengthening India's cultural diplomacy.

3. Heritage and Cultural Tourism

Major attractions include:

  • Forts

  • Palaces

  • Archaeological monuments

  • Museums

  • Heritage cities

  • Folk traditions

  • Regional festivals

  • Traditional cuisine

4. Wellness and Medical Tourism

India has become a preferred destination for:

  • Yoga

  • Ayurveda

  • Naturopathy

  • Traditional healing systems

  • Affordable and quality healthcare

The combination of ancient wellness traditions and modern medical facilities has enhanced India's global reputation.

5. Eco-tourism and Wildlife Tourism

Eco-tourism promotes responsible travel to natural areas, conserving biodiversity, supporting local communities, encouraging sustainable livelihoods, protecting wildlife habitats, and fostering environmental awareness through nature-based experiences.

Major attractions include:

  • National Parks

  • Tiger Reserves

  • Mangroves

  • Himalayan landscapes

  • Bird watching

  • Wildlife safaris

  • Trekking

  • Turtle conservation

  • Nature interpretation centres

6. Rural and Homestay Tourism

Rural and homestay tourism offers authentic village experiences, promotes local culture and handicrafts, generates sustainable livelihoods, empowers communities, and preserves traditional lifestyles through responsible travel.

Famous Rural & Homestay Tourism Destinations in India

  • Khonoma, Nagaland – India's first green village, community-based tourism.

  • Mawlynnong, Meghalaya – Known as one of Asia's cleanest villages.

  • Spiti Valley, Himachal Pradesh – Traditional Himalayan homestays.

  • Kumarakom, Kerala – Village homestays with backwater experiences.

  • Ziro Valley, Arunachal Pradesh – Apatani tribal culture and eco-tourism.

  • Chettinad, Tamil Nadu – Heritage mansions converted into homestays.

  • Kutch, Gujarat – Rural handicrafts and mud-house stays (Bhungas).

  • Majuli, Assam – River island with Satras and Assamese village life.

  • Hodka Village, Gujarat – Traditional Kutchi culture and community tourism.

  • Pochampally, Telangana – Famous for Ikat weaving and rural craft tourism.

7. MICE Tourism

India is emerging as a major destination for:

  • Meetings

  • Incentives

  • Conferences

  • Exhibitions

Modern convention centres and improved connectivity are helping diversify tourism beyond leisure travel.

G20 and Tourism Promotion

India's G20 Presidency significantly enhanced its tourism visibility.

Achievements

  • Over 200 G20 meetings conducted across 60+ cities.

  • Showcased India's culture, cuisine, heritage and destinations.

  • Promoted lesser-known tourist locations.

  • Strengthened India's global tourism branding.

  • Enhanced MICE tourism potential.

Coastal, Cruise and Adventure Tourism

Coastal, Cruise and Adventure Tourism: Promotes beaches, islands, cruise travel, water sports, trekking, rafting, desert safaris and adventure experiences, boosting visitor engagement and regional economies.

Infrastructure-Led Destination Development

The Government is shifting from developing individual attractions to creating integrated tourism ecosystems.

Major Schemes

1. Swadesh Darshan: A flagship Ministry of Tourism scheme developing integrated theme-based tourist circuits through quality infrastructure, improved connectivity, visitor amenities and sustainable destination development to enhance tourism experiences.

  • 76 projects sanctioned

  • 75 projects completed

  • Investment exceeding ₹25,295 crore

2. Swadesh Darshan 2.0: An upgraded destination-centric initiative focusing on sustainable, responsible and experience-based tourism by developing world-class infrastructure, enhancing destination competitiveness and improving visitor satisfaction.

  • 53 destination-centric projects

  • Worth ₹2,207 crore

3. PRASHAD Scheme: Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) develops pilgrimage destinations by improving infrastructure, heritage conservation, visitor facilities and accessibility for spiritual tourism.

  • 54 pilgrimage infrastructure projects

  • Worth ₹1,726 crore

4. SASCI: (Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment)

Provides financial assistance to States for developing tourism infrastructure, creating globally competitive destinations, improving connectivity, and strengthening visitor amenities to boost tourism-led economic growth.

  • 40 projects approved across 23 States

  • Investment of ₹3,295.76 crore

Challenge-Based Destination Development (CBDD)

  • 37 projects sanctioned

  • Worth ₹687.99 crore

These schemes focus on sustainable tourism infrastructure and integrated destination development.

Connectivity Improvements

Tourism accessibility has improved through:

  • Vande Bharat trains

  • Railway modernisation

  • UDAN regional air connectivity

  • Airport expansion

  • Better last-mile road connectivity

The Government has announced:

  • Development of 100 new airports

  • Expansion of 200 existing airports

These initiatives improve access to Tier-II and Tier-III destinations.

Sustainable Tourism

India is promoting tourism that is:

  • Environmentally responsible

  • Community-driven

  • Inclusive

  • Climate-resilient

  • Resource-efficient

Focus Areas of Sustainable Tourism

  • Travel for LiFE – Promote environmentally conscious travel.

  • Responsible Tourism – Minimise environmental and cultural impacts.

  • Nature Conservation – Protect biodiversity and ecosystems.

  • Local Employment – Generate livelihoods for communities.

  • Cultural Preservation – Safeguard heritage and traditions.

  • Community Participation – Involve local people in tourism.

  • Balanced Regional Development – Ensure inclusive growth across regions.

Tourism contributes to:

  • SDG 8: Decent Work & Economic Growth

  • SDG 9: Industry, Innovation & Infrastructure

  • SDG 12: Responsible Consumption & Production

  • SDG 14: Life Below Water (sustainable marine tourism)

Way Forward

India aims to become a globally competitive tourism destination by:

  • Developing high-value tourism infrastructure.

  • Strengthening digital tourism governance.

  • Promoting sustainable and inclusive tourism.

  • Enhancing connectivity to emerging destinations.

  • Supporting local communities and livelihoods.

  • Encouraging innovation and tourism entrepreneurship.

  • Preserving India's cultural and natural heritage while ensuring long-term economic growth.

India's tourism strategy combines heritage, sustainability, digital innovation and infrastructure to drive economic growth, generate employment, empower local communities and position the country as a globally competitive tourism destination.

articles.title: India on the Move: A Decade of Tourism-Led Growth (2014–2025)
articles.snippet: Discover how India transformed its tourism sector through infrastructure, digital reforms, sustainable initiatives, and flagship schemes, driving economic...
articles.fullTextHtml:
26 Jun 2026

Discover how India transformed its tourism sector through infrastructure, digital reforms, sustainable initiatives, and flagship schemes, driving economic growth while emerging as a leading global destination.

Syllabus Areas:

GS III - Economy, Environment and Tourism

The Press Information Bureau (PIB) has released a backgrounder titled "India on the Move – A Decade of Tourism-Led Growth", highlighting the remarkable transformation of India's tourism sector over the last decade. The report showcases the Government's initiatives to strengthen tourism infrastructure, improve connectivity, promote sustainable tourism, enhance digital services, and position India as a leading global tourism destination.

Tourism: A Driver of Inclusive Economic Growth

Tourism has evolved into a powerful engine of economic development, employment generation, regional growth, and cultural exchange.

Every tourist visit creates economic opportunities across multiple sectors, including:

  • Hotels and hospitality

  • Restaurants and local food businesses

  • Transport services

  • Tour guides

  • Handicrafts and artisans

  • Rural enterprises

  • Small and medium businesses

Tourism also promotes entrepreneurship, strengthens local economies, and enhances India's cultural diplomacy by showcasing the country's heritage and traditions to the world.

India's Tourism Growth in Numbers (2014–2025)

  • India has witnessed significant growth in both domestic and international tourism over the last decade.

  • Domestic Tourism: Approximately 2,277 crore domestic tourist visits were recorded during the period.

  • International Tourism: Between 2014 and 2025:

    • 181.25 million International Arrivals (including NRIs and foreign nationals)

    • 93.35 million Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs)

  • Foreign Exchange Earnings: Tourism generated approximately ₹21.61 lakh crore making it one of India's major sources of foreign exchange earnings.

Infrastructure Development:

1. Strengthening Tourism

Recognising that infrastructure forms the backbone of tourism, the Government has undertaken major investments in improving connectivity and visitor facilities.

Key developments include:

  • Expansion of national highways

  • Modernisation of railway stations

  • Construction of modern airports

  • UDAN regional air connectivity

  • Introduction of Vande Bharat trains

  • Improved last-mile connectivity

These initiatives have made tourist destinations more accessible while contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

2. Swadesh Darshan Scheme
About the Scheme

Launched in 2014, the Swadesh Darshan Scheme aims to develop integrated tourism infrastructure across identified tourist circuits.

Major Achievements

  • 76 projects sanctioned

  • Investment exceeding ₹5,000 crore

  • Spread across 15 thematic tourist circuits

  • 75 projects physically completed

Key Outcomes

  • Improved tourist amenities

  • Better road connectivity

  • Modern visitor facilities

  • Strengthened destination infrastructure

  • Enhanced tourism competitiveness

3. Swadesh Darshan 2.0

Introduced in 2022, Swadesh Darshan 2.0 shifts the focus from infrastructure creation to experience-based and sustainable tourism development.

Major Features

  • Sustainable destination development

  • Experiential tourism

  • Local community participation

  • Destination branding

Notable Projects

Tehri Lake, Uttarakhand

  • Floating log huts

  • Lakefront tourism experiences

Kurukshetra, Haryana

  • Mahabharata-themed attractions

  • Immersive cultural storytelling

4. PRASHAD Scheme
Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)

  • The objective is to develop and rejuvenate important pilgrimage destinations across India.

  • Achievements 54 projects sanctioned, Investment exceeding ₹1,700 crore

  • Major destinations include Somnath, Srisailam, Govardhan, Several other iconic pilgrimage centres

Benefits

  • Better pilgrim amenities

  • Improved safety and accessibility

  • Preservation of cultural heritage

  • Employment generation for local communities

Tourism Aligned with National Development

Tourism is increasingly being integrated with broader national development priorities.

Major focus areas include:

  • Development of the North-East

  • Rural tourism

  • Purvodaya States

  • Employment generation

  • Regional economic development

Recent Union Budget announcements have further strengthened investments in iconic tourism destinations.

Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI)

To create globally competitive tourism destinations, the Government launched the Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) programme.

Achievements

  • 40 projects sanctioned

  • Across 23 States

  • Total investment of ₹3,295.76 crore

Objectives

  • Develop world-class tourism hubs

  • Improve visitor experiences

  • Enhance destination competitiveness

  • Generate local employment opportunities

Sustainable Tourism: A New Growth Model

The Government is promoting tourism that balances economic growth with environmental conservation.

Major Focus Areas

  • Biodiversity conservation, Heritage preservation, Responsible tourism, Eco-friendly travel practices

Niche Tourism Products

  • Himalayan trekking trails, Birdwatching circuits, Turtle tourism, Eco-tourism destinations

Travel for LiFE

  • The Travel for LiFE initiative encourages tourists, businesses, and local communities to adopt environmentally responsible tourism practices and reduce ecological footprints.

Green Destination Initiatives

India's sustainable tourism efforts are receiving international recognition.

Major Achievement

Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram) became the first UNESCO World Heritage Site in South Asia to receive the Green Destinations Silver Certification.

Challenge-Based Destination Development (CBDD)

  • 38 projects approved

  • Total investment of ₹697.94 crore

Important projects include:

  • Panidihing Bird Sanctuary (Assam)

  • Nizam Sagar Eco-tourism Project (Telangana)

Tourism as an Instrument of Global Engagement

  • India's G20 Presidency highlighted the country's tourism potential before the international community.

  • The event showcased: India's heritage, Rich cultural traditions, Handicrafts, Tourism destinations

  • It also strengthened India's position in MICE Tourism, which includes: Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, Exhibitions

  • Tourism is increasingly serving as a tool for international cooperation, diplomacy, and cultural exchange.

India's Tourism Vision for the Future

India aims to become one of the world's leading tourism destinations.

Key Highlights

  • Ranked 8th among the world's top tourism economies

  • Tourism contributes approximately US$231.6 billion to India's economy

  • World Travel & Tourism Council (WTTC) projects India to become the 4th largest tourism economy over the next decade

  • More than 100 destinations upgraded through tourism infrastructure schemes

  • 50 key destinations proposed for world-class development

  • Revitalisation of the Incredible India campaign through digital promotion, international roadshows, and strategic partnerships

These initiatives seek to make India's tourism sector more resilient, globally competitive, sustainable, and inclusive.

India's tourism sector has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past decade through sustained investments in infrastructure, improved connectivity, digital governance, sustainability, and destination development. Programmes such as Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, SASCI, CBDD, and Travel for LiFE have expanded tourism opportunities while preserving India's rich cultural and natural heritage.

With ambitious plans under Viksit Bharat@2047, enhanced global outreach, and continued investments in human capital and infrastructure, India is steadily positioning itself as one of the world's most attractive and competitive tourism destinations.
